files_examined: patch_manager_mods/level_up_override_src/LevelUpOverride.cpp (grep hits: FileWatch.h include line 86, g_tableStamp line 374, LevelUpUi.h include line 2282)

findings.evidence: Line 117 now reads `filewatch::Stamp pageTable;` (previously uint64_t). The header never includes FileWatch.h; its only include is `#include "OptionsLogic.h"` at line 23. The header also uses g_tableStamp (lines 507, 584, 783), which is declared in LevelUpOverride.cpp:374, so the header compiles only because LevelUpOverride.cpp includes FileWatch.h at line 86 and includes LevelUpUi.h at line 2282, after both.
findings.suggested_investigation: Confirm that OptionsLogic.h does not transitively include FileWatch.h. If it does not, grep the whole mod directory for other includes of LevelUpUi.h besides LevelUpOverride.cpp:2282. Then compile a minimal TU that includes only LevelUpUi.h to see whether it fails. Also check that the Stamp != operator (used at line 783) is defined in FileWatch.h, since the contract test exercises == and != only at common_contract_test.cpp:194-204.
findings.why_it_matters: The header now depends on include order and on a translation-unit global it does not declare. Any new TU that includes LevelUpUi.h without first including FileWatch.h and defining g_tableStamp will fail to compile, or a future reorder of LevelUpOverride.cpp will break it. The contract test includes FileWatch.h but not LevelUpUi.h, so nothing guards this.

notes: The pageTable change itself is type-consistent: the assignments at lines 507 and 584 and the comparison at 783 use filewatch::Stamp against g_tableStamp, which is also a Stamp (LevelUpOverride.cpp:374, assigned at 625). No memset/memcpy of UiPanel was found in the header, so the non-trivial member type does not create a raw-byte copy hazard. The checker facts (build_check PASS, run_tests PASS) are consistent with this. Behaviour note: the page-close check at line 783 now compares the full Stamp rather than the previous uint64_t, so rewriting the table file with identical content may now close an open page. I did not verify the Stamp definition, so this is not reported as a finding. Scope: FileWatch.h and OptionsLogic.h were not read (not in the packet and not cited callees), so the include-chain conclusion relies on grep hits only."]
